sections.heading: EIP-8025 CFI Push at Tomorrow's ACDC
sections.summary: EIP-8025 will be proposed for CFI in Hegota at tomorrow's ACDC call; attendees urged to join and voice support.
sections.body:
- EIP-8025 is expected to be proposed for CFI (Considered for Inclusion) in Hegota at the next ACDC call (October 15).
- A short presentation (1–3 slides) will be prepared to highlight readiness and key arguments.
- The EIP-8025 document has been updated with the latest progress and arguments; the effort has been ongoing for a long time with many releases and refinements.
- Readiness is considered the strongest argument for CFI.
- All interested parties and EL client teams are encouraged to attend and speak up.
- Ignacio framed the ACDC call as a potentially important milestone for L1 block proving in protocol history.

sections.heading: EIP-7709 CFI and Execution Witness Simplification
sections.summary: EIP-7709 was CFI'd at the last ACDE call, removing the headers field from the execution witness by routing BLOCKHASH through the EIP-2935 system contract.
sections.body:
- EIP-7709 was CFI'd at the last ACDE call; it requires BLOCKHASH to use the EIP-2935 system contract instead of the header chain.
- This allows the `headers` field (up to 256 block headers) to be removed from the execution witness, since that data is now captured in the `state` field.
- The change simplifies execution witness generation, verification, and many edge-case tests (e.g., invalid header chains, parent hash mismatches).
- Long-term direction: when PVT arrives and bytecode is chunkified, the `code` field will also move into state, leaving the execution witness as primarily state tree nodes.
- CFI does not mean SFI, but it is a significant step forward.

sections.heading: Specs, Tests, and R2 Bucket Updates
sections.summary: ZKVM test release v21 targets Sepolia; a new long-lived R2 bucket provides 50k+ Sepolia stateless inputs for guest program testing.
sections.body:
- ZKVM test release version 21 is based on official Sepolia tests; the `public_keys` field was removed from stateless inputs as it is no longer relevant for performance and simplifies witness creation/verification.
- 13 PRs merged in the last two days adding test coverage, many motivated by real bugs found in guest programs; thanks to Gabriel and Omer for contributions.
- The execution specs branch has been heavily refactored to ease upstreaming; EIP-8025's PR is ~17,000 lines total, but only 56 lines touch the STF spec (the most sensitive part), with the bulk being testing framework changes and new tests.
- The Hive consumer now supports REST SSZ variant of the Engine API, enabling testing of execution witness generation in both JSON RPC and REST SSZ modes.
- A new test ZKVM benchmarks release targets current gas limits; benchmarks will also run on the EF proving cluster with 16 GPUs.
- A new R2 bucket for Sepolia stateless inputs is live with 50k+ blocks; this was the main source for bug discovery by CVM, CESU, and Nethermind.
  - The Sepolia R2 bucket will be long-lived, unlike previous devnet buckets.
  - Hoodi and Mainnet R2 buckets will follow as Glamsterdam activates on those chains.
  - Mainnet backfill for pre-Glamsterdam forks is a long-term intention but may require EL changes to generate execution witnesses.
- The updated EEST dashboard tracks EL compliance on execution witness construction and guest program compliance across supported ZKVMs.

sections.heading: Engine API: REST SSZ and Block Building EIPs
sections.summary: Nimbus has merged the REST SSZ engine API for new payload with witness; a companion EIP for get payload with witness has been drafted.
sections.body:
- An EIP defines the REST SSZ version of `engine_newPayloadWithWitness`; Nimbus has already implemented and merged it, visible on the EEST dashboard in both REST SSZ and JSON RPC modes.
- All other EL clients have draft PRs for the REST SSZ variant; they will appear on the dashboard once merged.
- A new companion EIP was created for the block building side (`getPayloadWithWitness`) to avoid re-execution of the block for witness generation.
  - Not strictly needed for EIP-8025 but part of the long-term mandatory proofs arc.
- EL teams are asked to thumbs-up the PR in the execution-APIs repo to help maintainers consider merging it.

sections.heading: ZKVM Standards: Testing, Security, and Formal Verification
sections.summary: Cody presented (via video) expanded RISC-V accelerator testing, a new randomness standard to mitigate hash-collision attacks, and progress on Zisk formal verification.
sections.body:
- RISC-V compliance testing has been expanded beyond the ISA standard to cover accelerators, memory acceleration, and the IO standard, using the ACT4 framework from the RISC-V community.
  - Tests are generated from Geth and the execution specs to verify accelerator correctness, not just interface existence.
  - Good progress but significant compliance gaps remain; teams are encouraged to address them.
  - Proposal: new standards should ship with a test suite by the time they are accepted.
- A hash-collision attack vector was identified by Łukasz (Nethermind): unseeded internal hash maps in guest programs could be exploited to attack all provers for a given zkEVM simultaneously.
  - A new standard formalizes Łukasz's proposal to provide a host facility for sampling fresh randomness per execution, with no proving overhead.
  - Accompanying tests and a demo implementation for OpenVM are available.
  - [Cody's slides](https://codygunton.github.io/talks-and-writing/2026-10-14-zkevm-breakout)
- Zisk formal verification (Lean-based) has been hardened via stress testing of constraints; missing links ("welds") were identified and tied together, and assumptions were removed from the main soundness theorem.
  - A handoff meeting with Zisk took place regarding long-term formal verification as part of a broader initiative.
  - Covers RISC-V circuits only (not recursion layers); clear path to stronger guarantees via tracked GitHub issues.
- SoundCalc (bits-of-security calculator for zkVMs) gained STIR support; a Lean version is in progress from Symbolic Software.

sections.heading: Proving Infrastructure: ere and Prover Tooling
sections.summary: Hans' Prover tool extends BenchmarkCore for GPU proving clusters; ere gains profiling support and peak memory reporting for guest programs.
sections.body:
- Prover is a Terraform extension to BenchmarkCore that abstracts multi-machine, multi-GPU proving cluster orchestration.
  - Designed so that generating proofs on complex clusters (e.g., 4 machines with GPUs) is as easy as running benchmarks on a single machine.
- ere is gaining profiling support, enabling the prover frontend to show where proving cost is concentrated in guest programs.
- Peak memory usage per benchmark case will be reported, important because zkVMs have hard memory caps.
- Goal: a single dashboard showing proving time, proving cost, and disaggregated cost breakdown.
- Benchmarks can run in emulation mode for cost estimation, with plans to also run on the EF proving cluster with 16 GPUs for real proving-time numbers.
- Hans (out of office) will demo the UI in the next call.

sections.heading: CL Consensus Spec Refinements and Optional Proofs EIP
sections.summary: The proof engine scope was reduced to verification only; a new draft EIP proposes recursive chain proofs for bandwidth-efficient sync from the weak subjectivity checkpoint.
sections.body:
- Two main PRs refined the consensus specs:
  - Refactored the proof data type and gossip validation handler to use the new code-based gossip handler framework (previously prose-only).
  - Reduced the proof engine scope to exclusively proof verification (previously also handled proof generation requests and fetching); client teams have optionality on implementation (embedded verifier vs. external HTTP sidecar).
- A new draft EIP proposes extending proof scope to attest to chain subsets via recursive proofs:
  - Each proof takes one new payload extending the chain head plus the ancestor (parent) proof, forming a recursive chain back to the origin.
  - Would allow syncing from the weak subjectivity checkpoint to the head using a single proof (or K-of-N proofs), reducing bandwidth and execution requirements by orders of magnitude.
  - Open questions around completeness (what if a proof cannot be generated) and other edge cases.
  - [Francesco's slides](https://frisitano.github.io/slides/decks/optional-proofs-2026-10-14/index.html?v=20261014133540#2)
- CL specs have been rebased on the Gloas (Glamsterdam) specs; ready for Sepolia deployment.

sections.heading: Prysm and Lighthouse: EIP-8025 CL Implementation Status
sections.summary: Prysm has a working proof-of-concept using go-ere for proof verification; Lighthouse merged proof engine sidecar support into Unstable and can run without an EL.
sections.body:
- Prysm implemented EIP-8025 as a proof of concept: [PR #17690](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17690).
  - Uses [go-ere](https://github.com/nalepae/go-ere) as a library (function call, no sidecar) for proof verification, directly included in the Prysm Beacon node binary.
  - Works on Kurtosis with Prysm prover and verifier nodes.
  - Running a verifier node on Sepolia; briefly connects with Lighthouse peers, but there is an incompatibility: Lighthouse sends proofs of type 0, which is undefined, causing Prysm to reject the message and disconnect the peer.
- Lighthouse has merged EIP-8025 proof engine sidecar support into Unstable.
  - Maintains an external sidecar so development is not gated on the Lighthouse release cycle; plan is to eventually integrate verifiers into the codebase once things stabilize.
  - Unstable Lighthouse can run without an EL (acknowledged as controversial).
  - Lion is also working on the recursive proofs effort with Tau: a PR to pass the block root, a new route to get leaves for optimized state hashing on ZK Boost.

sections.heading: Sepolia Deployment Plans and Beacon API Open Questions
sections.summary: EF plans to deploy a prover on Sepolia and invite CL teams; open questions remain on the Beacon API GET method and SSZ container types.
sections.body:
- EF intends to deploy a prover on Sepolia and is inviting client teams to join the network for testing.
- Guest programs and proof stacks to be used have not been decided; a collaborative rotation of proof stacks and guest programs is proposed for coverage.
- Beacon API open questions:
  - Most clients have only implemented the method for submitting proofs to the Beacon node; a GET method is needed for the Dora Explorer use case.
  - EIP-8025 specifies no storage requirement for execution proofs on the Beacon node; Lighthouse's fork currently serves proofs from the gossip cache.
  - PandaOps team is working on indexing and query optimizations on their side.
  - SSZ container types for the new payload request need further discussion; PRs have been opened in the consensus specs.
- Francesco will share a Kurtosis config file with Manu for local devnet testing of Lighthouse + Prysm interoperability.

sections.heading: Zilkworm Guest Client: ere Integration, Performance, and MFBD Witness Format
sections.summary: Zilkworm reported ~half Reth's proving cost, a third fewer cycles between Alpha 2 and Alpha 4, and its MFBD flat witness format.
sections.body:
- **ere benchmark integration**: Zilkworm was first integrated in June using legacy fixtures; after the benchmark moved to canonical EEST fixtures only, Zilkworm re-integrated via ere guests with two draft PRs (Alpha 4 release registration and re-adding Zilkworm to the benchmark).
  - Passes the entire test-zkEVM suite except two fixtures in a family where Reth also has known failures; matches every Sepolia block.
  - Approximately 50% of Reth's estimated proving cost, cheaper on every block.
  - CI release pipeline rechecks all results on every release.
  - Alpha 5 will natively read canonical stateless input bytes format, removing the fixture adapter; draft PRs will come out of draft.
- **Performance gains (Alpha 2 → Alpha 4)**: cut one-third of executed cycles despite Alpha 4 doing more work (additional pre-validation).
  - Custom `memcopy` and `memmove` implementations yielded significant gains due to RISC-V's no-unaligned-access constraint; compilers don't handle this well.
  - Byte swap overhead (EVM is big-endian, RISC-V is little-endian): the `bswap` emulation function was the top hot function, exceeding EVM execution time; forced inlining as a partial workaround; Zisk is thought to have added a byte swap instruction extension.
  - JUMPDEST analysis takes ~11% of all execution cycles (up to 30% of EVM bytecode execution); fine-tuned but limited by lack of vector instructions; Zisk is thought to have added a precompile for this.
  - Compiler options: code size is essentially free in SP1, so aggressive inlining and loop unrolling improve performance; some dead ends documented.
  - LLVM scheduling tuning for interpreter-like VM execution (changes compilation trade-offs) noted as an external initiative.
- **z6m node (specialized execution client)**: achieves 300 ms payload-to-witness timing, 2.2 seconds block-timestamp-to-witness on average.
  - Current EL clients take 5–9+ seconds to produce a witness before provers start.
  - Uses ~1 TB storage, optimized for witness generation speed rather than disk efficiency.
  - Includes Erigon integration for transaction pool blobs.
- **Prover benchmarks**: Airbender V3 integration achieved ~3.8 seconds with two RTX 5090s (trailing ~20% behind zkSync OS); SP1 at ~35 seconds with a single GPU on Alpha 4.
- **MFBD flat witness format**: zero-decode, zero-allocation design where witness bytes are reinterpret-cast into flat object pointers.
  - Uses a minimally perfect hash function (MPHF) with a simple mixer (~25 instructions: shifts, XORs, multiply) and a collision sidebar for edge cases.
  - Shortened keys used (not full 32-byte hashes) since addresses and hashes are already randomized on honest blocks.
  - Maps: address→plain state, hash→code, RLP→node RLP for the node store; bundled into a "direct state" container.
  - Grid MPT loop combines pre-state and post-state trie validation in a single pass using a stack-based approach.
  - Structural and functional sanitization checks (alignment, bounds, HEAD-AC matching, absence proof verification).
  - An alternative hash-state implementation consuming canonical stateless input bytes directly runs at 1.11× the cycles of DirectState (~11% slower).
  - [Blog post on MFBD design](https://zilkworm.hashnode.dev/introducing-mfbd-a-minimally-perfect-hash-based-flat-witness-format-for-zkevms)
- Zilkworm is now fully open source (as of ~2–3 weeks ago), with all CI, releases, PRs, and reviews public.
- Airbender V3 security: reportedly offers 100-bit security (up from 80-bit); whether provable or conjectured is uncertain.
- Francesco suggested pushing Zilkworm's optimizations upstream to Silkworm, or finding a forum to discuss them in more detail.
